title: The days of the week
description: Say which day it is, and when things happen.

explanation.summary: The seven days are masculine nouns, and Spanish has no capital letters for them. With a day you normally leave the article out, which makes the day a time rather than a thing.

sections.heading: The days
sections.body: Lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado and domingo. They are all masculine, so el lunes is right, but you leave the el out when you are talking about a time: el lunes comemos pollo, but lunes comemos pollo. The two days that take an el when you name the thing are el sábado and el domingo when you mean the day itself.

examples.en: On Monday I have a meeting.
On Sunday I do not work.

sections.heading: Saying the time
sections.body: Es la una, es la dos, es la tres. After la una you say la una y media, but after any other hour you say las dos y media. For a quarter past, es la dos y cuarto; for half past, y media; for a quarter to, es la dos y cuarto para las tres.

examples.en: It is a quarter past three.

sections.heading: What time is it on
sections.body: A time of day uses a feminine word, not a masculine one: por la mañana, por la tarde, por la noche. A day of the week is masculine. That difference catches people out.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: The days are masculine and take el, but you usually leave the article out: el lunes, but lunes por la mañana.
Masculine: el lunes. It is also plural in meaning: los lunes.

exercises.translation: on Monday I have a meeting
exercises.note: The article comes when you name the day.
